cues.en: This is the Global News podcast from the BBC World Service.
cues.zh: 这里是BBC世界服务的《全球新闻》播客。

cues.en: I'm Charlotte Gallagher, and in the early hours of Thursday, the 1st of October, these are our main stories.
cues.zh: 我是夏洛特·加拉格尔。10月1日星期四凌晨，以下是本节目的主要新闻。

cues.en: Passengers on a flight to Israel describe how they overpowered the co-pilot
cues.zh: 一架飞往以色列的航班上，乘客讲述了他们如何制服副驾驶；

cues.en: after he stabbed the pilot and apparently tried to crash the plane.
cues.zh: 这名副驾驶刺伤机长后，显然试图让飞机坠毁。

cues.en: And new data shows Switzerland's glaciers lost more than 5%
cues.zh: 新数据显示，瑞士冰川今年损失了超过5%的冰量，

cues.en: of their ice this year as a result of climate change.
cues.zh: 原因是气候变化。

cues.en: Also in this podcast, how adults and children use different senses to perceive emotions,
cues.zh: 本期还将讨论，成年人和儿童如何用不同感官感知情绪，

cues.en: and why AI has resurrected the Hollywood actress Greta Garbo.
cues.zh: 以及人工智能为何让好莱坞女演员葛丽泰·嘉宝重现。

cues.en: Zero friction, remarkable speed.
cues.zh: 零摩擦，速度惊人。

cues.en: We look at the ethics of so-called ghostploitation.
cues.zh: 我们将探讨所谓“亡灵剥削”的伦理问题。

cues.en: Israeli passengers who were caught up in terrifying scenes on a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv
cues.zh: 在从迪拜飞往特拉维夫的航班上经历恐怖场面的以色列乘客，

cues.en: have made an emotional return home to Ben Gurion Airport.
cues.zh: 激动地返回了本·古里安机场。

cues.en: The co-pilot stabbed the pilot and apparently attempted to crash the plane,
cues.zh: 副驾驶刺伤机长，并显然试图让飞机坠毁；

cues.en: which plummeted 5,000 metres in 2 minutes.
cues.zh: 飞机在两分钟内骤降5000米。

cues.en: Passengers then stormed the cockpit to subdue the attacker, and the plane was safely diverted to Saudi Arabia
cues.zh: 随后乘客冲进驾驶舱制服袭击者，飞机在安全转向沙特阿拉伯；

cues.en: by off-duty pilots who were on the flight.
cues.zh: 由同机的休班飞行员操控。

cues.en: The co-pilot who launched the attack has been arrested and is being questioned by Saudi authorities.
cues.zh: 发动袭击的副驾驶已被逮捕，正接受沙特当局讯问。

cues.en: The injured pilot is reported to be in a stable condition in hospital,
cues.zh: 据报道，受伤机长在医院情况稳定，

cues.en: but there are still many unanswered questions.
cues.zh: 但仍有许多问题没有答案。

cues.en: No information has been released about the identity of the attacker or how he was able to have access to a weapon on board.
cues.zh: 目前尚未公布袭击者身份，也不清楚他如何能够在机上接触到武器。

cues.en: Our correspondent Yoav Zitun reports from Tel Aviv.
cues.zh: 本台记者约阿夫·齐顿从特拉维夫发回报道。

cues.en: In Tel Aviv, families began arriving at the airport once they were told their loved ones
cues.zh: 在特拉维夫，得知亲人即将从沙特回国后，家属开始抵达机场；

cues.en: were on their way home from Saudi Arabia.
cues.zh: 亲人正在从沙特返家。

cues.en: When the passengers landed, Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met them.
cues.zh: 乘客抵达后，以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡接见了他们。

cues.en: Some of them said the pilot who was stabbed managed to open the cockpit door despite his injuries.
cues.zh: 一些乘客说，被刺伤的机长尽管身负伤势，仍设法打开了驾驶舱门。

cues.en: Israel has identified him as Indian national Smit Machchhar.
cues.zh: 以色列确认他是印度籍人士斯米特·马奇哈尔。

cues.en: Finally, late in the evening, the passengers came out of the airport.
cues.zh: 当天深夜，乘客终于走出机场。

cues.en: Asaf Rajwan, who tackled the attacker, got a hero's welcome. I didn't think about it.
cues.zh: 制服袭击者的阿萨夫·拉伊万受到英雄般的欢迎。“我当时没有想太多。”

cues.en: It's, you know, it's just something that you do without thinking,
cues.zh: 这就是一种下意识的行动，

cues.en: just run into there and save your daughter's life,
cues.zh: 冲进去，救下你女儿的性命，

cues.en: your family, wife, and all the people in the plane.
cues.zh: 以及你的家人、妻子和飞机上的所有人。

cues.en: You don't think, you don't think, you just act.
cues.zh: 你不会思考，不会多想，只会行动。

cues.en: Moti Kona, another passenger, described his terrifying experience.
cues.zh: 另一名乘客莫蒂·科纳讲述了自己的恐怖经历。

cues.en: In my life, I've never seen death pass before my eyes. It was a frightening situation.
cues.zh: 我这辈子从未见过死亡从眼前掠过，那是令人恐惧的处境。

cues.en: The plane was swerving from side to side. At one stage, there were no pilots.
cues.zh: 飞机左右摇摆。有一度，驾驶舱里没有飞行员。

cues.en: One was neutralized and the other was in shock.
cues.zh: 一人被制服，另一人陷入震惊。

cues.en: Today there is much joy and celebration here.
cues.zh: 今天这里充满喜悦和庆祝。

cues.en: Tomorrow a search for answers must begin.
cues.zh: 明天必须开始寻找答案。

cues.en: The attack has prompted strong political reaction ahead of a hugely consequential election
cues.zh: 这起袭击引发了强烈的政治反应，而以色列本月晚些时候将举行一场影响重大的选举；

cues.en: in Israel later this month.
cues.zh: 选举将在本月晚些时候举行。

cues.en: As I heard from our Middle East specialist Sebastian Usher, the Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was on the ropes.
cues.zh: 正如我从中东事务专家塞巴斯蒂安·厄舍尔那里听到的，以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡正处于困境。

cues.en: He'd always presented himself as Mr. Security, and of course, on his watch, the 7th of October happened.
cues.zh: 他一直把自己塑造成“安全先生”，当然，在他的任期内发生了10月7日事件。

cues.en: He has not allowed an independent investigation to take place.
cues.zh: 他一直没有允许展开独立调查。

cues.en: A lot of pressure from his rivals to do that, so he was in a difficult situation.
cues.zh: 他的对手施加了很大压力要求调查，因此他处境艰难。

cues.en: I think this makes the situation easier for now, at least. Obviously, it's a diversion.
cues.zh: 我认为至少目前这让局势变得容易应对一些。显然，这是一种转移注意力。

cues.en: It had nothing to do with him, but it ended well as far as Israel is concerned.
cues.zh: 这与他毫无关系，但就以色列而言，结果是好的。

cues.en: But he will benefit from that. This could have been a terrible disaster, obviously.
cues.zh: 但他会从中受益。显然，这本可能是一场可怕的灾难。

cues.en: And I think the messaging that he's trying to get across and his supporters trying to get across came through when he was at the airport.
cues.zh: 我认为，他和支持者试图传达的信息，在他出现在机场时已经传达出来。

cues.en: He was meeting the Israelis who were on the plane when they came back.
cues.zh: 飞机上的以色列乘客回来时，他正在机场迎接他们。

cues.en: And one of them, the passenger who says that he was one of those who was able to get into the cockpit and wrestle with the co-pilot, even said he took control of the plane briefly.
cues.zh: 其中一名乘客说，自己是设法进入驾驶舱并与副驾驶搏斗的人之一；他甚至说自己曾短暂控制飞机。

cues.en: He'd seen how to do it on TV.
cues.zh: 他是在电视上看到过操作方法。

cues.en: He greeted Mr. Netanyahu and was greeted by the Israeli prime minister as kind of equals
cues.zh: 他向内塔尼亚胡先生致意，以色列总理也像对待平等的人一样回应他；

cues.en: and used the same phraseology that Mr. Netanyahu has used a lot—that he rose like a lion essentially to the challenge—
cues.zh: 他还使用了内塔尼亚胡经常使用的说法：他像狮子一样迎接挑战；

cues.en: and this is something that echoes what Mr. Netanyahu used just last week at the UN General Assembly
cues.zh: 这呼应了内塔尼亚胡上周在联合国大会上使用的话；

cues.en: and very much in support of his strategy that Israel must not stop its fight until it's defeated its enemies.
cues.zh: 也非常支持他的战略：以色列必须继续战斗，直到击败敌人。

cues.en: He's received criticism from political rivals, but he's making political capital out of this.
cues.zh: 他受到政治对手的批评，但也在借此积累政治资本。

cues.en: The opposition leader Yair Lapid said that what happened with this flight
cues.zh: 反对党领袖亚伊尔·拉皮德说，这趟航班发生的事

cues.en: had nothing to do with what Mr. Netanyahu warned about a day ago, when he said there might be a major attack.
cues.zh: 与内塔尼亚胡先生一天前警告可能发生重大袭击毫无关系。

cues.en: He said you can't use it this way. This was different.
cues.zh: 他的意思是不能这样利用这件事。这完全是另一回事。

cues.en: You did not say this was going to happen, so don't try and play it up as if it was.
cues.zh: 你并没有说这会发生，所以别把它说得好像真是那回事。

cues.en: And they're now talking about more stringent checks for pilots.
cues.zh: 他们现在还在讨论加强对飞行员的检查。

cues.en: And cabin crew going to Israel, because going there as a passenger, you go through a lot of checks.
cues.zh: 前往以色列的机组人员也会受到关注，因为乘客前往那里要经过多重检查。

cues.en: But presumably they'll now tighten the checks they carry out on staff. One hundred percent.
cues.zh: 但现在他们可能会收紧对机组人员的检查，百分之百会这样。

cues.en: I mean, I think, you know, we know that if you're travelling on an Israeli airline, it's incredibly stringent.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，如果你乘坐以色列航空公司的航班，安检会极其严格。

cues.en: They have air marshals; they have probably the highest security in the world.
cues.zh: 他们配有空警，安保水平可能是世界最高的。

cues.en: The issue is planes that are carrying Israelis but are not Israeli planes.
cues.zh: 问题在于，有些飞机载着以色列人，却不是以色列的飞机。

cues.en: You don't have the same stringent security now.
cues.zh: 这些飞机目前没有同样严格的安保。

cues.en: Obviously, Israel does have, you know, as much control as it can over that, but it doesn't have final say.
cues.zh: 显然，以色列会尽可能加以控制，但它没有最终决定权。

cues.en: So what has been announced by the Israeli authorities is they're going to try.
cues.zh: 所以，以色列当局宣布，他们会尝试这样做。

cues.en: I don't know quite how they're going to do it, but bring that sort of level of control into non-Israeli airlines as well.
cues.zh: 我不太清楚他们会怎么做，但会把这种程度的管控也带到非以色列航空公司。

cues.en: I think that will be very difficult: you can't put air marshals on every plane going there.
cues.zh: 我认为这会很困难，因为不可能在每架飞往那里的飞机上都安排空警等人员。

cues.en: And as you say, focusing on the air crew as well, more perhaps than before.
cues.zh: 正如你所说，他们也会比以前更加关注机组人员。

cues.en: But I think across the political divide in Israel there's unity about
cues.zh: 但我认为，在以色列的政治阵营之间，大家都同意

cues.en: praising the passengers on board as great heroes, and that security needs to be increased,
cues.zh: 应该称赞机上乘客是英雄，并加强安保，

cues.en: but division over how this is going to play out politically.
cues.zh: 但对于政治上会如何发展，大家存在分歧。

cues.en: As I say, Netanyahu's political rivals can see that this is doing him good at the moment.
cues.zh: 正如我所说，内塔尼亚胡的政治对手看得出，这件事目前对他有利。

cues.en: This could potentially see him over the line. We'll have to see.
cues.zh: 这可能帮助他越过胜选门槛，但还要拭目以待。

cues.en: Sebastian Usher. New data reveals Switzerland's glaciers suffered a near-record loss of ice
cues.zh: 塞巴斯蒂安·厄舍尔。新数据显示，瑞士冰川的冰量损失接近历史纪录，

cues.en: this year as intense summer heat waves led to unusually rapid melting.
cues.zh: 今年夏季的强烈热浪导致冰层异常快速消融。

cues.en: The figures from Glacier Monitoring Switzerland have been called devastating by experts.
cues.zh: 瑞士冰川监测机构的数据被专家称为灾难性的。

cues.en: Our correspondent Imogen Foulkes told us more.
cues.zh: 我们的记者伊莫金·福尔克斯为我们详细介绍。

cues.en: The key findings for this year are that the glaciers have lost another five and a half percent of their volume.
cues.zh: 今年的主要发现是，冰川体积又减少了百分之五点五。

cues.en: That's almost the same. We had a record loss in 2022, close to 6%.
cues.zh: 这几乎相同。2022年的损失创下纪录，接近百分之六。

cues.en: And if you look at the last five years, these glaciers have lost 20%, a fifth of their volume.
cues.zh: 过去五年里，这些冰川损失了百分之二十，也就是体积的五分之一。

cues.en: And the bigger ones this year, your listeners might know the Rhône Glacier or the Aletsch,
cues.zh: 至于今年较大的冰川，听众可能知道罗讷冰川或阿莱奇冰川，

cues.en: this summer, with these successive heat waves, they have lost more than ever.
cues.zh: 它们在今年夏天经历连续热浪，损失的冰量超过以往。

cues.en: Now some people might be saying, well, why does that really matter?
cues.zh: 有人可能会问，山顶上的冰，这真的有什么关系？

cues.en: Ice on the top of a mountain.
cues.zh: 不过是山顶上的冰而已。

cues.en: I've been talking to Matthias Huss, who's the head of glacier monitoring here in Switzerland.
cues.zh: 我采访了马蒂亚斯·胡斯，他是瑞士冰川监测部门负责人。

cues.en: The long-term consequence is water shortage.
cues.zh: 长期后果将是缺水。

cues.en: We're not seeing it now because we're still getting a lot of water from the glaciers during these heat waves.
cues.zh: 我们现在还没有看到这种情况，因为热浪期间冰川仍会释放大量水。

cues.en: But if you repeat the same year 20 years from now, it will be much more critical in terms of water availability
cues.zh: 但如果二十年后再出现同样的一年，水资源供应将变得严峻得多，

cues.en: for irrigation, the food supply.
cues.zh: 影响灌溉和粮食供应。

cues.en: It's also all the transportation chains; nuclear power plants sometimes need to close down
cues.zh: 交通运输链也会受到影响；核电站有时不得不关闭，

cues.en: because the streams simply don't have enough water.
cues.zh: 因为溪流里的水实在不够。

cues.en: So it's really changing the whole situation.
cues.zh: 所以，这确实正在改变整个局面。

cues.en: Imagine the Alps are known for glaciers, but what could the future look like?
cues.zh: 想想看，阿尔卑斯山以冰川闻名，但未来会是什么样？

cues.en: Well, this is actually the thing that everybody in this part of the world is asking themselves.
cues.zh: 这正是这一地区每个人都在问自己的问题。

cues.en: Just two weeks ago, I drove up over the Alps from Italy.
cues.zh: 就在两周前，我从意大利驾车翻越了阿尔卑斯山。

cues.en: It's a trip I do almost every year in September,
cues.zh: 我几乎每年九月都会走这趟路，

cues.en: and this is the first time I have seen no snow, no ice, everything grey.
cues.zh: 但这是我第一次看到没有雪、没有冰，一切都是灰色的。

cues.en: Now Matthias Huss spends every year from June till September way up in the high Alps measuring the ice.
cues.zh: 马蒂亚斯·胡斯每年六月到九月都会深入高山阿尔卑斯测量冰层。

cues.en: This year he found a really different landscape.
cues.zh: 今年，他发现了截然不同的景观。

cues.en: I've just visited a large plateau that is now completely devoid of ice.
cues.zh: 我刚参观了一片如今完全没有冰的巨大高原。

cues.en: It's a moon landscape, dry and dead.
cues.zh: 那里像月球表面，干燥而死寂。

cues.en: There are some little remnants, some ice blocks still lying around and melting there on the hot rocks.
cues.zh: 还有一些残留物，冰块仍散落在炙热的岩石上融化。

cues.en: And interestingly, also the vegetation is coming back and trying to recolonize these deserts.
cues.zh: 有趣的是，植被也在恢复，试图重新占据这些荒地。

cues.en: So it's a shifting of the elevation boundaries.
cues.zh: 所以，海拔边界正在发生位移。

cues.en: The ice is getting lost and the vegetation is rising.
cues.zh: 冰层正在消失，植被则向更高处扩展。

cues.en: There we go, beautiful views that we all know about in the Alps, but these views are changing.
cues.zh: 阿尔卑斯山那些美丽的景色仍在眼前，但景色正在改变。

cues.en: And as we heard there from Matthias Huss, from the report published today, the consequences are going to be much more
cues.zh: 正如我们从马蒂亚斯·胡斯和今天发布的报告中听到的，后果将远不止

cues.en: than the postcards we send home from holiday in the Alps. The Alps are changing.
cues.zh: 我们从阿尔卑斯山度假时寄回家的明信片所展现的。阿尔卑斯山正在改变。

cues.en: Imogen Foulkes. The X2 roller coaster at California's Six Flags Magic Mountain theme park
cues.zh: 伊莫金·福尔克斯。加州六旗魔术山主题公园的X2过山车

cues.en: has been one of America's most popular rides, but it's now closing for good
cues.zh: 曾是美国最受欢迎的游乐设施之一，但如今将永久关闭，

cues.en: after more than 100 people came forward alleging they suffered brain injuries after riding it.
cues.zh: 此前有超过100人站出来，称乘坐后遭受脑部损伤。

cues.en: The park said the roller coaster had passed a range of safety tests, but conceded that visitors had lost confidence in the attraction.
cues.zh: 公园方面称，这座过山车通过了一系列安全测试，但承认游客已经对这项游乐设施失去了信心。

cues.en: CNN journalist Kyung Lah has been investigating.
cues.zh: CNN记者Kyung Lah一直在进行调查。

cues.en: What the families or the victims themselves have described is that they have gone into the hospital.
cues.zh: 家属或受害者本人描述说，他们曾经住进医院。

cues.en: They had their skulls cut open, and their lawyers say that it was connected.
cues.zh: 他们的头骨被切开，而他们的律师称，这与过山车有关。

cues.en: They believe it was connected to this ride, three people that I saw.
cues.zh: 他们认为这与这项游乐设施有关；我见到了其中三个人。

cues.en: One was very small and young. The other woman was a little larger and ten years older.
cues.zh: 一个人年纪很小，也很年轻；另一位女性稍年长一些，大了十岁。

cues.en: So we have a 25-year-old woman, one who is 39, and then an older gentleman, probably in his sixties.
cues.zh: 所以，一位是25岁的女性，另一位是39岁，还有一位年长男士，大概六十多岁。

cues.en: And he was quite larger. So three very different types of people, different bodies and different ages.
cues.zh: 而那位男士身材相当高大。三个人的体型和年龄都很不相同。

cues.en: America correspondent Shaimaa Khalil told us more about the ride.
cues.zh: 美国记者Shaimaa Khalil向我们进一步介绍了这项游乐设施。

cues.en: You only have to look at YouTube: people filming themselves as they're sitting on those seats that rotate 360 degrees.
cues.zh: 只要看看YouTube就知道了：人们拍下自己坐在那些会旋转360度的座椅上的画面。

cues.en: They've been pulled backwards in that beginning of the ride.
cues.zh: 在游乐设施启动时，他们会被向后拉。

cues.en: And then cut into the, you know, the money shot of them plunging down head first.
cues.zh: 随后进入那个你知道的精彩镜头：他们头朝下俯冲而下。

cues.en: In some cases, lawyers have mentioned some needing emergency brain surgery.
cues.zh: 律师提到，在一些案例中，有人需要接受紧急脑部手术。

cues.en: You mentioned the 100 riders alleging brain injuries.
cues.zh: 你提到了100名声称遭受脑部损伤的乘客。

cues.en: But one law firm bringing several cases against the park said it was contacted by over 400 people.
cues.zh: 但一家针对该公园提起多起诉讼的律师事务所称，有超过400人联系过他们。

cues.en: They reported broader injuries they say are connected to the ride.
cues.zh: 这些人报告了更广泛的伤情，并称伤情与这项游乐设施有关。

cues.en: And while the lawyers have said their clients welcome the closure, it has come too late for some of them. This has been going on for a while.
cues.zh: 律师们说，他们的客户欢迎关停，但对其中一些人来说，这来得太晚了。这种情况已经持续一段时间了。

cues.en: We know of one family of a 22-year-old who died after riding the X2 about two years ago.
cues.zh: 我们知道，有一个家庭的22岁家人在大约两年前乘坐X2后去世。

cues.en: They had just settled a wrongful death case with the park in August.
cues.zh: 他们直到8月才与公园就这起过失致死案达成和解。

cues.en: So it has been going on for a while. Troubles with that very popular ride.
cues.zh: 所以，这已经持续一段时间了，是那项非常受欢迎的游乐设施出了问题。

cues.en: The park said they recognize that trust in that particular ride has just been dented.
cues.zh: 公园方面称，他们认识到，游客对这项游乐设施的信任已经受损。

cues.en: It's been affected, and they've taken that very seriously.
cues.zh: 信任受到了影响，而他们对此高度重视。

cues.en: They did reiterate: this is a very popular ride. It has passed a range of safety tests.
cues.zh: 他们确实再次强调：这是一项非常受欢迎的游乐设施，也通过了一系列安全测试。

cues.en: I would say, though, that we're talking about permanently closing that ride.
cues.zh: 不过我想说的是，我们谈论的是永久关闭这项游乐设施。

cues.en: It had been under investigation since July, so it's been closed since July.
cues.zh: 它从7月起就一直在接受调查，因此也从7月起关闭。

cues.en: After reports of two riders suffering brain haemorrhages, California safety regulatory officials have been investigating.
cues.zh: 在有报道称两名乘客出现脑出血后，加州安全监管官员一直在调查。

cues.en: The park says that 16 million people have ridden the X2 since it was relaunched in 2008.
cues.zh: 公园方面称，自X2于2008年重新开放以来，已有1600万人乘坐过。

cues.en: So yes, it's very popular. Yes, it's really an adrenaline rush and a real favourite among enthusiasts.
cues.zh: 所以，它确实非常受欢迎。它确实令人肾上腺素飙升，也是爱好者的最爱。

cues.en: But lawyers say some clients had gone in for a thrill.
cues.zh: 但律师说，一些客户原本只是为了寻求刺激。

cues.en: But they've suffered catastrophic brain injuries, and these are the things that are still ongoing.
cues.zh: 但他们遭受了灾难性的脑部损伤，而这些情况仍在持续。

cues.en: That have led to the permanent closure. Shaimaa Khalil.
cues.zh: 这些情况最终导致了永久关停。Shaimaa Khalil报道。

cues.en: Next, it's one of the most famous lines in cinema.
cues.zh: 接下来，这是电影史上最著名的台词之一。

cues.en: I want to be alone. Where have you been? I suppose I can cancel the Vienna contract.
cues.zh: 我想一个人待着。你去哪儿了？我想我可以取消维也纳的合同。

cues.en: I just want to be alone. You're going to be very much alone, my dear madam. This is the end.
cues.zh: 我只是想一个人待着。你会彻底孤独的，亲爱的女士。这就是结局。

cues.en: Greta Garbo in the 1932 film Grand Hotel.
cues.zh: 这是葛丽泰·嘉宝在1932年电影《大饭店》中的台词。

cues.en: But now the star has gone from the golden age of Hollywood to the new age of artificial intelligence.
cues.zh: 但如今，这位明星已经从好莱坞黄金时代走进了人工智能的新时代。

cues.en: More than a century after her screen debut and decades after her death.
cues.zh: 她首次登上银幕已有一个多世纪，去世也已有数十年。

cues.en: An AI version of the actress has starred in an advertisement for ball bearings.
cues.zh: 这位女演员的人工智能版本出演了一则滚珠轴承广告。

cues.en: Zero friction, remarkable speed. And it can be paid for like it's 1919 with your energy savings.
cues.zh: 零摩擦，速度惊人。而且你可以用节省的能源费用来支付，就像回到了1919年。

cues.en: Now, if you don't mind, I want to be alone.
cues.zh: 现在，如果你不介意的话，我想一个人待着。

cues.en: The rationale behind the ad is that when alive, Garbo featured in a promotional film for the same company.
cues.zh: 这则广告的依据是，嘉宝在世时曾出演过这家公司的宣传片。

cues.en: But the reappearance of an actress who retired in her 30s and lived much of her life as a recluse has raised eyebrows.
cues.zh: 但这位三十多岁便息影、人生大部分时间过着隐居生活的女演员再次出现，引发了质疑。

cues.en: Other late stars have also been given the AI resurrection treatment, and it's been labelled by some as ghostploitation.
cues.zh: 其他已故明星也接受了人工智能复活式处理，有人将其称为“亡灵剥削”。

cues.en: Dominic Lees is an associate professor of filmmaking at Britain's Reading University who specialises in generative AI.
cues.zh: Dominic Lees是英国雷丁大学电影制作副教授，专门研究生成式人工智能。

cues.en: He says it's an ethical dilemma. It's in a very murky legal zone.
cues.zh: 他说，这是一个伦理困境，也处在非常模糊的法律地带。

cues.en: The big questions are who controls us after we're dead, and law internationally is yet to work out those questions.
cues.zh: 关键问题是：我们死后由谁控制我们，而国际法律还需要解决这些问题。

cues.en: Who controls our voice, who controls our faces and our images?
cues.zh: 谁控制我们的声音，谁控制我们的面孔和形象？

cues.en: We've got a new situation in which a celebrity's estate
cues.zh: 我们面临一种新情况：名人的遗产管理机构

cues.en: No longer just handles the financial affairs and so on after their death.
cues.zh: 在名人去世后，它不再只是处理财务事务等事宜。

cues.en: But now controls their likeness and can deploy that for financial gain.
cues.zh: 如今，它还控制名人的肖像，并可以将其用于谋取经济利益。

cues.en: And that would not have been something that Greta Garbo was aware of when her executors were appointed.
cues.zh: 而在她的遗嘱执行人获任命时，这并不是葛丽泰·嘉宝能够预见的事情。

cues.en: This is a huge question for the creative industries and for performers.
cues.zh: 这对创意产业和表演者来说是一个重大问题。

cues.en: We found that in the UK, voice actors have lost 70 or 80% of their income in the last couple of years.
cues.zh: 我们发现，在英国，配音演员过去几年收入减少了70%或80%。

cues.en: Because of the advent of voice cloning.
cues.zh: 原因是语音克隆技术的出现。

cues.en: And now we're moving on to the point where an actor's likeness can be reproduced visually.
cues.zh: 现在我们正走向这样一个阶段：演员的肖像可以被视觉化地复制。

cues.en: So this is a new situation we're encountering. Dominic Lees.
cues.zh: 所以，这是我们正在面对的新情况。多米尼克·利斯。

cues.en: Still to come in this podcast.
cues.zh: 本期播客接下来还有更多内容。

cues.en: We see a strong, robust face with prominent brow ridges, but many features are remarkably similar to ours.
cues.zh: 我们看到一张坚实、强健的面孔，眉脊突出，但许多特征与我们惊人地相似。

cues.en: Scientists digitally reconstruct the face of a human from more than 300,000 years ago.
cues.zh: 科学家用数字技术重建一名30多万年前人类的面貌。

cues.en: This is the Global News podcast.
cues.zh: 这里是《全球新闻》播客。

cues.en: Russia's president Vladimir Putin will deliver his annual foreign policy speech today.
cues.zh: 俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京今天将发表年度外交政策演说。

cues.en: It will be closely watched for any signs and signals from the Kremlin
cues.zh: 人们将密切关注克里姆林宫释放的任何迹象和信号，

cues.en: about its war on Ukraine and about escalating tensions between Moscow and Europe.
cues.zh: 看它对乌克兰战争以及莫斯科与欧洲日益紧张关系的态度。

cues.en: Our Russia editor Steve Rosenberg will be there in the hall.
cues.zh: 我们的俄罗斯事务编辑史蒂夫·罗森伯格将在现场。

cues.en: He says all signals point to the conflict continuing.
cues.zh: 他说，所有信号都表明冲突仍将继续。

cues.en: Down at the Russian parliament, the standing ovation for President Putin is expected.
cues.zh: 在俄罗斯议会，人们预计会起立鼓掌欢迎普京总统。

cues.en: After an election his critics say was neither free nor fair, his supporters dominate the new Duma.
cues.zh: 在一场批评者称既不自由也不公正的选举后，他的支持者控制了新一届国家杜马。

cues.en: But Putin knows that in Russia, he's the one who runs the show, not them.
cues.zh: 但普京知道，在俄罗斯，真正掌控局面的是他，而不是他们。

cues.en: So what decisions will he take on Ukraine and on tensions with Europe?
cues.zh: 那么，他将如何处理乌克兰问题和与欧洲的紧张关系？

cues.en: Will there be olive branches or escalation?
cues.zh: 局势会出现橄榄枝，还是升级？

cues.en: This week, I've been searching for clues. Steve Rosenberg, BBC News.
cues.zh: 本周我一直在寻找线索。史蒂夫·罗森伯格，BBC新闻。

cues.en: Clue number one, my brief encounter with Russia's foreign minister.
cues.zh: 线索一：我与俄罗斯外交部长的短暂会面。

cues.en: He doesn't sound very conciliatory.
cues.zh: 他的语气听起来并不友善。

cues.en: When I ask Sergey Lavrov, is Russia waging a hybrid war on Europe, he doesn't deny it.
cues.zh: 我问谢尔盖·拉夫罗夫，俄罗斯是否在对欧洲发动混合战争；他没有否认。

cues.en: By hybrid war, do you mean Russia
cues.zh: 你所说的混合战争，是指俄罗斯

cues.en: destroying drones and missiles that Britain and Europe are supplying Ukraine with?
cues.zh: 摧毁英国和欧洲提供给乌克兰的无人机和导弹吗？

cues.en: He says, call it what you want: this is a war Europe is waging against us. No mention that Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
cues.zh: 他说，你爱怎么称呼都行，这是欧洲对我们发动的战争。他没有提到，是俄罗斯在2022年发动了对乌克兰的全面入侵。

cues.en: Mr Lavrov goes on to accuse the West
cues.zh: 拉夫罗夫还指责西方

cues.en: of using brute force in Venezuela,
cues.zh: 在委内瑞拉使用武力，

cues.en: in Iran.
cues.zh: 以及在伊朗使用武力。

cues.en: When I point out that Russia uses brute force every day in Ukraine,
cues.zh: 当我指出俄罗斯每天都在乌克兰使用武力时，

cues.en: he doesn't deny that either.
cues.zh: 他同样没有否认。

cues.en: He says it's to eliminate a direct threat to Russia.
cues.zh: 他说，这是为了消除对俄罗斯的直接威胁。

cues.en: Peace feels a long way away, especially after my next conversation.
cues.zh: 和平感觉遥不可及，尤其是在我接下来的谈话之后。

cues.en: We shall finish off Ukraine as a viable state sooner or later.
cues.zh: 我们迟早会终结乌克兰作为一个可行国家的存在。

cues.en: Sergey Karaganov is a veteran foreign policy strategist.
cues.zh: 谢尔盖·卡拉加诺夫是一名资深外交政策战略家。

cues.en: He's also honorary chairman of Russia's Council for Foreign and Defence Policy.
cues.zh: 他还是俄罗斯外交与国防政策委员会的名誉主席。

cues.en: We'll not occupy all over the territory of Ukraine.
cues.zh: 我们不会占领整个乌克兰领土。

cues.en: We'll create a no-fly and non-militarized zone, central and western parts of Ukraine.
cues.zh: 我们将在乌克兰中部和西部建立禁飞区和非军事区。

cues.en: And if they do not agree, they will suffer.
cues.zh: 如果他们不同意，就会遭受苦难。

cues.en: That's not acceptable to Kiev, it's not acceptable to Europe, and it seems not acceptable to America.
cues.zh: 这对基辅不可接受，对欧洲不可接受，看来对美国也不可接受。

cues.en: Well, that's a problem. Then we'll have to go further.
cues.zh: 那么，这是个问题。我们就得进一步行动。

cues.en: And according to my scenarios, the first series of blows will be conventional.
cues.zh: 根据我的设想，第一轮打击将使用常规武器。

cues.en: But if Europe does not surrender, then unfortunately we'll have to go nuclear.
cues.zh: 但如果欧洲不投降，很遗憾，我们就不得不动用核武器。

cues.en: There will be little left of some European countries.
cues.zh: 一些欧洲国家将所剩无几。

cues.en: We've heard nuclear sabre-rattling before from Moscow, and plenty of it over the last four and a half years.
cues.zh: 过去我们听到过莫斯科的核威胁，最近四年半更是屡屡如此。

cues.en: Much of it has felt like an attempt to scare Europe into scaling back support for Ukraine.
cues.zh: 其中许多听起来像是在吓唬欧洲，让它减少对乌克兰的支持。

cues.en: It comes and goes, but never disappears completely.
cues.zh: 这种威胁时有时无，却从未完全消失。

cues.en: This week, Russia sent a letter to NATO, threatening to use nuclear weapons
cues.zh: 本周，俄罗斯致信北约，威胁要使用核武器，

cues.en: if any attempt was made to cut off its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad.
cues.zh: 如果有人试图切断其波罗的海飞地加里宁格勒。

cues.en: NATO's response: stop the nuclear threats.
cues.zh: 北约回应：停止核威胁。

cues.en: So there is no sign of de-escalation.
cues.zh: 所以没有任何缓和迹象。

cues.en: And yet so many Russians I speak to about the war and about tensions with Europe
cues.zh: 然而，我谈到战争和与欧洲的紧张关系时，许多俄罗斯人

cues.en: seem to want to pretend that none of this is happening.
cues.zh: 似乎想假装这一切都没有发生。

cues.en: People like Tatyana.
cues.zh: 比如塔季扬娜。

cues.en: The big part of nation don't want to think about this situation. They want to escape these thoughts.
cues.zh: 这个国家的大多数人不想思考这种局面，他们想逃避这些念头。

cues.en: And maybe it's easy way to live because we don't think this horrible time every day.
cues.zh: 也许这样生活更容易，因为我们不必每天想着这段可怕的时期。

cues.en: Back in the Duma, President Putin is about to finish his speech.
cues.zh: 回到国家杜马，普京总统即将结束演说。

cues.en: His war on Ukraine has not gone to plan.
cues.zh: 他对乌克兰发动的战争没有按计划进行。

cues.en: And yet the Kremlin leader seems confident and in control, and determined
cues.zh: 然而，这位克里姆林宫领导人似乎自信且掌控局面，并决心

cues.en: not to give any ground on any front.
cues.zh: 在任何战线上都不让步。

cues.en: Steve Rosenberg.
cues.zh: 史蒂夫·罗森伯格报道。

cues.en: How do you work out how someone is feeling or if you're in danger?
cues.zh: 你如何判断一个人的感受，或判断自己是否处于危险中？

cues.en: Research from Durham University in the UK has found that adults and children rely on different senses to judge people and situations.
cues.zh: 英国杜伦大学的研究发现，成人和儿童依靠不同感官来判断他人和情境。

cues.en: The study was led by psychology professor Paddy Ross. He outlined his findings to Claudia Hammond.
cues.zh: 这项研究由心理学教授帕迪·罗斯主持。他向克劳迪娅·哈蒙德介绍了研究发现。

cues.en: There was a study back in the 70s called the Colavita study,
cues.zh: 上世纪70年代有一项名为科拉维塔研究的实验，

cues.en: in which if you saw a flash, you were meant to hit a button,
cues.zh: 实验中，如果你看到闪光，就要按下一个按钮，

cues.en: and if you heard a beep, you were meant to hit a different button.
cues.zh: 如果听到哔声，就要按下另一个按钮。

cues.en: But then what the experimenters did was on purpose played them both at the same time
cues.zh: 但随后，实验人员故意让两种刺激同时出现，

cues.en: and just said to people, hit whatever button you fancy.
cues.zh: 只对参与者说：想按哪个按钮就按哪个。

cues.en: And what they found was that predominantly adults hit the button for the flash, so the visual stimulus,
cues.zh: 他们发现，成人大多按下代表闪光、也就是视觉刺激的按钮，

cues.en: but they found the reverse in kids, that the children would primarily hit the button for the beep.
cues.zh: 但儿童的情况相反，他们主要按下代表哔声的按钮。

cues.en: So we wanted to know whether that Colavita effect extended to emotion recognition.
cues.zh: 因此，我们想知道科拉维塔效应是否也适用于情绪识别。

cues.en: So what we did was we showed kids and adults
cues.zh: 于是，我们让儿童和成人观看

cues.en: people moving in emotional ways, so maybe cowering in fear or with their fists up in anger.
cues.zh: 人们以表达情绪的方式活动，比如因害怕而蜷缩，或愤怒地举起拳头。

cues.en: But we played mismatched auditory stimuli, so someone was crying or laughing or shouting.
cues.zh: 但我们播放了不匹配的听觉刺激，比如有人在哭、笑或喊叫。

cues.en: And what happens is, if you show someone, for instance, cowering in fear, but you hear them laughing,
cues.zh: 如果你让参与者看到一个人因恐惧而蜷缩，却听到这个人在笑，结果会怎样呢？

cues.en: and you just say to participants, ‘How is that person feeling?’
cues.zh: 然后你只问参与者：“那个人感觉如何？”

cues.en: An adult will tend to say what they see: that the person's fearful, that they're scared.
cues.zh: 成年人往往会根据看到的内容回答：那个人很害怕、受到了惊吓。

cues.en: Whereas for exactly the same stimulus, a child will say that that person's happy if they hear them laughing.
cues.zh: 但面对完全相同的刺激，如果听到笑声，孩子会说那个人很开心。

cues.en: Why could it be? It seems really surprising.
cues.zh: 为什么会这样？这确实令人非常意外。

cues.en: You'd think that the most salient, obvious thing in front of you would be what someone's looking like.
cues.zh: 你可能会以为，眼前最突出、最明显的东西应该是那个人的外表。

cues.en: We know that the auditory system is the first to develop.
cues.zh: 我们知道，听觉系统是最先发育的。

cues.en: There's evidence of people being able to hear in utero.
cues.zh: 有证据表明，人类在子宫内就能够听见声音。

cues.en: So there's some studies where children will attend longer to their mother's voice
cues.zh: 有研究发现，孩子听到母亲的声音时会专注更久，

cues.en: Compared with a stranger reading the same thing, after hearing her in the womb.
cues.zh: 相比陌生人朗读同样内容，因为他们在子宫里听过母亲的声音。

cues.en: You know, children are little. They cannot see as far as someone who is 5 ft tall.
cues.zh: 孩子个子小，视线达不到一个五英尺高的成年人那么远。

cues.en: We as adults can see threat before we hear it. We can see much further. We are taller.
cues.zh: 成年人能在听到威胁之前先看见它；我们看得更远，因为我们更高。

cues.en: We have better eyesight than babies can; they can't see more than a few feet in front of their faces.
cues.zh: 我们的视力比婴儿好；婴儿看不清面前几英尺以外的东西。

cues.en: So I suppose they're exposed to all of this auditory stimuli.
cues.zh: 所以我想，他们会接触到所有这些听觉刺激。

cues.en: You can't really ignore what you're hearing. So it could be
cues.zh: 你很难真正忽略听到的东西。所以，这可能是

cues.en: an experience thing: that is what they are most experienced at doing, listening compared to seeing.
cues.zh: 经验造成的：相比看，他们更习惯于听。

cues.en: But it could be a fun evolutionary argument that actually it's much more
cues.zh: 不过，也可以从有趣的进化论角度解释：从生存角度看，

cues.en: useful from a survival point of view when you're young to be able to hear threat before you can see
cues.zh: 年幼时，能在看见威胁之前先听见它，可能更有用。

cues.en: it. Do we know what's going on in the brain that makes this happen?
cues.zh: 它。我们知道大脑中是什么机制导致这种情况吗？

cues.en: There's two schools of thought. One is that it's a thing called overshadowing,
cues.zh: 有两种理论。一种认为，这是一种叫作“遮蔽效应”的现象，

cues.en: which is where the kids are hearing something and seeing something, but they're processing that auditory information
cues.zh: 孩子同时听到、看到某种信息，但他们处理听觉信息的程度

cues.en: much, much more, so to speak, than the visual. And so when they go to recall
cues.zh: 远远超过视觉信息。因此，当他们回忆

cues.en: what they've seen, they just have access to way more auditory information than visual information.
cues.zh: 自己看见的东西时，能够调用的听觉信息远多于视觉信息。

cues.en: The other school of thought is something called response competition, and that's where they process both signals just fine,
cues.zh: 另一种理论叫“反应竞争”，认为他们其实能很好地处理两种信号，

cues.en: but when they get asked then to make a response, they just rely on what they hear
cues.zh: 但当被要求作出回答时，他们只依赖听到的内容，

cues.en: for whatever reason. Maybe it's a more salient emotional cue for them.
cues.zh: 原因不明。也许对他们来说，听觉是更突出的情绪线索。

cues.en: Professor Paddy Ross.
cues.zh: 帕迪·罗斯教授。

cues.en: Finally, scientists have pieced together what one of the world's first humans looked like, using fossil fragments to bring them to life in a new digital image.
cues.zh: 最后，科学家利用化石碎片拼出了世界上最早的人类之一的面貌，并以新的数字图像让他重现。

cues.en: The male face had been reconstructed after more than 300,000 years.
cues.zh: 这张男性面孔是在三十多万年后重建出来的。

cues.en: Scientists initially thought the remains, which were discovered in Morocco, belonged to a Neanderthal, but
cues.zh: 科学家最初认为，在摩洛哥发现的遗骸属于尼安德特人，但

cues.en: a reappraisal in 2017 showed it was the earliest Homo sapiens recorded.
cues.zh: 2017年的重新评估表明，这是有记录以来最早的智人。

cues.en: Professor Francesco Galassi from Italy's University of Pavia co-authored the groundbreaking study.
cues.zh: 意大利帕维亚大学的弗朗切斯科·加拉西教授是这项突破性研究的共同作者。

cues.en: I would say that what struck us was how recognisably human the face looked.
cues.zh: 我想说，最让我们震撼的是，这张脸看起来是如此明显的人类面孔。

cues.en: We see a strong, robust face with prominent brow ridges, but many features are remarkably similar to ours.
cues.zh: 这是一张强健结实的脸，有突出的眉脊，但许多特征与我们惊人地相似。

cues.en: The brain case still has a more archaic shape.
cues.zh: 不过，颅脑仍呈现更为古老的形状。

cues.en: Seeing the face on the screen brought us remarkably close to humans who lived more than 300,000 years ago.
cues.zh: 在屏幕上看到这张脸，让我们真切接近了三十多万年前生活的人类。

cues.en: Our story begins at Jebel Irhoud in Morocco, where the first skull was discovered during mining activities.
cues.zh: 我们的故事始于摩洛哥的伊尔胡德山；第一具头骨是在采矿活动中发现的。

cues.en: Later excavations uncovered more human fossils, stone tools and, above all, evidence of fire.
cues.zh: 之后的发掘发现了更多人类化石、石器，最重要的是火的证据。

cues.en: Heated flint tools from the site were dated to around 315,000 years ago.
cues.zh: 该遗址的加热燧石工具经测定距今约31.5万年。

cues.en: These discoveries revealed a very early stage in the evolution of Homo sapiens.
cues.zh: 这些发现揭示了智人演化中一个非常早期的阶段。

cues.en: This is particularly important because until a few years ago it was thought that Homo sapiens was
cues.zh: 这尤其重要，因为直到几年前，人们还认为智人的出现时间

cues.en: much more recent than these findings appear to suggest.
cues.zh: 比这些发现所显示的要晚得多。

cues.en: Bringing back to life the face of one of our ancestors is very important
cues.zh: 让我们一位祖先的面孔重现，意义非常重大，

cues.en: both scientifically and in terms of the popularization of science.
cues.zh: 无论对科学研究还是科学普及都是如此。

cues.en: Of course, there are some important limitations that we need to consider because we are not reconstructing
cues.zh: 当然，我们也必须考虑一些重要局限，因为我们重建的并不是

cues.en: just one complete individual. Ours is a digital skull which is a composite, so we should not
cues.zh: 某一个完整的个体。这是一个数字化的复合头骨，所以不应

cues.en: think of this as an exact portrait of one person.
cues.zh: 把它看作某一个人的精确肖像。

cues.en: We should call it an anatomically informed approximation of a
cues.zh: 我们应该称之为一名伊尔胡德

cues.en: Jebel Irhoud individual. So we are bringing back to life
cues.zh: 个体的、基于解剖学信息的近似形象。因此，我们让

cues.en: somebody—or, let's say, the anatomy of a potential individual from that site, from that prehistoric period.
cues.zh: 某个人——或者说，让那个遗址、那个史前时期潜在个体的解剖结构重现。

cues.en: Professor Francesco Galassi.
cues.zh: 弗朗切斯科·加拉西教授。

cues.en: And that's all from us for now. If you want
cues.zh: 今天的节目就到这里。如果你想

cues.en: to get in touch, you can email us at globalpodcast@bbc.co.uk.
cues.zh: 联系我们，可以发送邮件至 globalpodcast@bbc.co.uk。

cues.zh: 本期《全球新闻播客》由丽贝卡·米勒混音。

cues.en: The editor is Karen Martin and I'm Charlotte Gallagher.
cues.zh: 编辑是凯伦·马丁，我是夏洛特·加拉格尔。

cues.en: Until next time, goodbye.
cues.zh: 下期再见。
